intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-413#diagnose-dashboard-ci-probe-flakes (plan 885, slice 2), revision 88810b6a9c883d99ecf8e8f60ef697f6b525db7c.

Promise: a blank or whitespace-only keyboard Start presents the started session's terminal exactly once, with the correct session, the Start control, and takesKeyboard false. The refused-admission retry likewise presents it exactly once, with takesKeyboard true.

Verdict: ASSERTION GAP (the "exactly once" part).

Fault (caller's suggestion, validated): in dashboard/src/askedLaunches.ts, right after `page.onLaunched(record);` in the launched-outcome effect, I added `setTimeout(() => { console.log('IC-FAULT duplicate presentation'); page.onLaunched(record); }, 50);`. This is a duplicate presentation that arrives in a later task than the first one. Fixtures and assertions were not changed.

Maintained checks examined, in dashboard/frontend-tests/launches/responsive-unattached-startup.spec.ts:
- `await expect.poll(() => presentTerminal.mock.calls).toHaveLength(1)` in the blank/whitespace test.each (line 166)
- the same poll in "a refused default admission lets Start repeat..." (line 242)
- the session, control and takesKeyboard checks on calls[0] that follow each poll

Runs (from the isolated scratch worktree, using the focused command `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard:frontend -- responsive-unattached-startup.spec.ts`; load averages about 4.1 / 5.4 / 11.2):
- Baseline: 4 tests passed, exit 0.
- Faulted: 4 tests passed, exit 0. The IC-FAULT log appeared during both test.each cases, so the faulted path was reached. The poll takes the first length-1 sample, and the test ends before the second call arrives.
- Independent witness: a scratch copy of the spec (ic-witness.spec.ts, deleted afterwards) waits 300 ms after each length-1 poll and logs the call count. It logged "IC-WITNESS calls 2" for the blank case, the whitespace-only case and the refused-admission retry, while all its tests still passed. That confirms the terminal was presented twice on all three examined paths and the maintained assertions did not catch it.
- Restored: I reverted askedLaunches.ts with git checkout and deleted the witness. `git status --short` was empty, matching the clean pre-probe state. The same command passed again (4 passed, exit 0). The scratch worktree was then removed with git worktree remove.

Not tested: dropping the presentation entirely. The poll would time out on length 1 there, so that fault was not the more telling one.

Next proof action (left to the caller): make the "exactly once" check hold after the presentation settles. For example, after the first call, wait on a later observable state that comes after any further presentation would happen, then assert the count is still 1. A fixed sleep in the test would not do this. Apply it to the test.each and to the refused-admission retry.

Prior disposition: slice 2 deliberately replaced the synchronous toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) with a poll to fix a flake. The gap found here is a side effect of that change. This probe does not make a repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Vitest "Duration"): baseline 2.67 s, faulted 2.04 s, restored 2.53 s. The witness run was similar (Duration not captured). Each npm command took about 3.6 s wall time, plus npm ci (not timed).
- Human effort: not available. No human took part in this delegated run.
- Agent effort: not available. No separately supported token or turn measure was available to this agent.
- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 57197 ms (measured), from 1795789877000 to 1795789934197 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision 88810b6a9. Verdict: assertion gap on "exactly once". Decision: record it with no follow-up (developer decision, 2026-11-27). Rationale: the synchronous check the repair replaced would also have read one call before a duplicate arriving a task later, so the gap predates the change. The product presents once per settled launch, clearing the page's attempt before calling `onLaunched`. The component has no observable state after presentation that could rule out an arbitrarily delayed duplicate without a fixed sleep.
